column3: Immediate parallel: knowingly saying a lie against God within People of the Book.
Tongues formulate false labels and thereby fabricate a lie against God.
V12 preserves a parallel bodily-turning reading, while its rejected route remains contrast only.
Knowledgeable concealment of truth by a party given the Book sharpens the knowing clause.
Same local Book-address: mixing truth with falsehood and concealing truth knowingly.
Contrasts sound handling of the Book with following ambiguous portions for fitnah and interpretation.
Degrees before God does not clarify tongue, Book, or false attribution.
Knowingly swearing a lie supplies a related form of deliberate false speech.
False invention against God is relevant, though without the Book-and-tongue mechanism.
Mistaken self-assessment of guidance is only a broad contrast to false presentation.
Same local group plans a staged public profession and retraction around revelation.
Tongues describe falsely in a related attribution scene, but lacks the Book claim.
Hidden hostility behind a stated profession is a limited speech-versus-interior parallel.
The Book's covenant restricts speech about God to truth; they have studied its contents.
Directly names fabrication of a lie against God.
A contrary People-of-the-Book example: belief and non-sale of God's signs.
The verse concerns facing death, not textual or verbal attribution.
Tongues and mouths circulate what is not known, while treating it lightly before God.
A false association claim is related only at the level of speaking about God.
Direct parallel: words displaced from their places and tongues twisted in religious attack.
Creation signs do not add to the charge of textual misattribution.
An outward declaration is followed by a privately devised statement contrary to it.
False assignment to God is adjacent, but not the Book-and-tongue question.
The statement that it is not jest does not illuminate 3:78's mechanism.
Turning away is a lexical bodily parallel, not a textual-speech parallel.
A party hears God's speech, then alters it after understanding, knowingly.
The mention of David's and Jesus's tongues does not bear on false attribution.
Direct fabrication against God is relevant; the verse centers its final accounting.
This self-statement has no material link to the Book or false speech.
A genuine statement that something is from God supplies a contrary attribution example.
The claimed sonship statement is a concrete false saying about God.
Professed belief followed by turning away gives a general profession-versus-reality contrast.
Denial of the sonship claim reinforces a contrary boundary on speech about God.
Denial of the Book and messages is related opposition, not misattribution.
The verse joins invented claims to an eventual questioning, without a textual claim.
Holding fast to the Book is a contrary model to manipulating its claimed content.
Claims about who is better guided are related speech, but not Book falsification.
Writing and justice in debt documentation are too distant from the Book claim.
Tongues say what hearts do not contain, a close oral-versus-inner-reality parallel.
Oaths asserting group membership are a limited false-claim parallel.
Clarifying Jesus's human life does not address textual attribution.
Tongues bearing witness concerns accountability, not the alleged Book content.
Reviving earth and clarified signs do not explain the focus verse.
Recitation and worship guidance do not add to the false-attribution scene.
Rejection and future news are only a broad response-to-message parallel.
Divine sufficiency against attempted deception is not a textual handling parallel.
Degrees, forgiveness, and mercy do not clarify 3:78.
Turning or evading in the command of justice offers a secondary use of the turning verb.
The recollection of upbringing does not add to the focus verse.
Closest material parallel: writing a book by hand, then saying it is from God.
Fear of being called false is a reversed accusation, not a false attribution.
Given the Book, a party casts God's Book behind its backs as if unaware.
The alleged sonship statement specifies the false claim continued by the surrounding passage.
Rejection of a recognized confirming Book differs from claiming words are in it.
Filial piety does not bear on textual or verbal falsification.
Lack of knowledge of the Book and mere conjecture supplies a nearby contrast to knowing falsification.
The call to prostration does not clarify 3:78.
Explicitly denies that the Quran can be fabricated and calls it confirmation and Book-detail.
Repentance at death does not add to the focus verse.
Same surah: recipients of a Book are called to God's Book, then a party turns away.
The command to grant respite adds no textual or speech relation.
Competing dismissive claims while reciting the Book give a distant Book-and-speech context.
God's creative word counters the sonship fabrication attributed in the passage.
Offers a criterion for the claim that a text is from God: absence of much contradiction.
A hostile accusation about the messenger is a contrast to the focus verse's accusation against God.
After truth is clear, some People of the Book seek to turn believers back; contextual opposition.
Ranks in striving do not clarify textual distortion or attribution.
Even a tangible written book would be called manifest magic; a contrary reception of writing.
Intercession's shares do not add to the focus verse.
Pairs fabrication against God with denial of His signs and its consequence.
Same surah: disagreement after knowledge among recipients of the Book provides immediate context.
Warns against hardened hearts among prior Book recipients; only broad contextual relevance.
Teaching the Book and wisdom is a general positive counterpoint to misuse of the Book.
Knowledge of the Book and witness language does not address false attribution.
Challenges claimants to produce a more guiding Book from God, preserving a true-source criterion.
The Book's recipients and questioning response are only remotely related.
Selective belief in the Book is a different failure of Book reception.
Divine revelation of Book and wisdom contrasts with a group's attempt to mislead.
The messenger's non-withholding of the unseen does not clarify 3:78.
Calls People of the Book to uphold their scriptures and what came from their Lord.
False or harmful teaching around what is recited is related, but not a claim inserted into the Book.
From yourselves is only a contrary attribution formula.
Denial and turning from God's signs are broader than the focus's false claim.
A specific false statement about God supplies a substantive but secondary parallel.
Knowledge that something is truth from their Lord is contextual, without speech distortion.
A false omen-attribution before God is only a remote attribution parallel.
Rejecting or killing messengers is a broader pattern, not alteration of Book speech.
The shared charge to Book recipients supplies only general scriptural context.
The bare statement that they say something has no specified relevance.
The calendar in God's Book does not illuminate false textual attribution.
The Book's coherent, paired character is a broad positive contrast to misrepresentation.
Faith and loyalty do not clarify tongue, Book, or attribution.
Mutual blame and idolatry do not add to the focus verse.
The description of eating from a tree is unrelated.
Plotting against the messenger is unrelated to textual false attribution.
What was fabricated vanishes at fulfillment; a late consequence parallel only.
The marking on the nose is unrelated.
Warning by revelation and refusal to hear do not clarify 3:78.
Guidance and rejection of association lack a specific textual-speech connection.
The command not to obey deniers adds no specific relation.
Directly prohibits mixing truth with falsehood and concealing truth while knowing.
Condemns concealing clarified proofs and guidance after their disclosure in the Book.
Directly joins concealment of what God sent down in the Book with selling it cheaply.
Treats a cheap exchange of God's covenant and false oaths as a related misuse of divine commitment.
A Book-covenant requires making it clear rather than concealing it.
Addresses People of the Book and restricts speech about God to truth.
Names distortion of words from their places and forgetting part of what was recalled.
Names concealment of much of the Book, countered by making clear what had been hidden.
Repeats the displacement of words from their positions in a setting of false speech.
Pairs forging a lie against God with denial of His signs.
Explicitly includes claiming revelation and speaking falsely about God.
A group substitutes a saying other than what was said to them, a close alteration-of-utterance parallel.
Trading God's signs for a small price gives a motive-pattern parallel to misusing revelation.
Directly condemns forging a lie against God or denying His signs.
Those who forge lies against God are publicly identified in the accounting scene.
Defines lying invention against God through denial of His signs.
Forbids pursuing or voicing what lacks knowledge; a restraint parallel to 3:78.
Denies knowledge for a grave utterance transmitted from predecessors.
Calls the claimants of a divine associate fabricators of a lie against God.
Forbidding invention of a lie against God is central to its warning.
Commands avoidance of false speech, supplying a general contrary norm.
Records the charge that the message is fabricated, a reversed accusation parallel.
Directly condemns one who forges a lie against God or denies truth when it comes.
Pairs forging a lie against God with rejecting truth after it arrives.
Frames the accusation that the messenger fabricated against God and answers it by divine sealing and truth-establishment.
A false claim about God's angels shows another form of ungrounded divine attribution.
Denies knowledge behind a claim and characterizes it as following conjecture.
Directly names the gravest wrong as forging a lie against God while being called to submission.
Those charged with the Torah but not carrying it provide a Book-handling contrast.
Hypothetical fabrication of sayings against God receives an emphatic rebuttal.
